claims.text: One writer and one reader per endpoint with role-prefixed keys: writer.write throws on a reused key and keeps every key ever written in a Set, so a long-lived worker or socket accumulates one string per call forever, a leak that grows with call count. So either per-call isolation (channel ids as plugin ids, as rpc-channels plans) or unbounded retention.

claims.text: The transport fixes, made in transport before S4 and frozen as its rpc-facing surface: (a) delete the key from the writer's `keys` Set when it settles (keys stay unique because rpc uses a monotonic call id, even for initiator and odd for the peer), removing the per-call leak; (b) a reader-to-writer cancel path, which rpc carries as its own control message and calls writer.cancel with; (c) 3 or more plugin test cases (a plugin value in a call, in a stream chunk, and after cancel). rpc keeps default per-key refs, never sharedRefs: a channel in a value is a seroval plugin that writes only the channel id, and the endpoint's own channel table, not seroval refs, resolves the id on the other side. No envelope allocation: rpc demuxes on message[0], passing transport tuples (types 0 to 2) to the reader unchanged and sending its own control messages (call-less ones: credit, cancel, hello, close) with types 3 and up; the method name rides inside the call value as [name, args], one extra array per call, not per record.

claims.text: Conceded: O9 (API churn) and the envelope part of O10, given P10 and S3.

P10 fixes only the writer's keys Set. The reader keeps one slot per key in its slots Map after the value settles (read.ts onEnd sets SETTLED, never deletes) and only reader.cancel(key) removes it, so a long-lived endpoint still leaks one slot (promise, resolvers) per call and per result unless rpc calls reader.cancel on every settled key. cancel on an OPEN key also adds to the cancelled Set, which empties only on a terminal message or end(), so a peer that never sends one leaks the key. The 'about 50 lines' of P13 does not cover this reader side; rpc must own the call to cancel after each settle, plus a test with 10,000 sequential calls checking Map sizes.
